follow100Note: $0.94 of the $11.00 kept belongs to noncontrolling partners — $10.07 is Disney shareholders'.
footerNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,327M, Sports $1,393M, Experiences $2,250M (before corporate costs). Of the $2,855M of net income, $243M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $2,612M is attributable to Disney shareholders.
oneTimers: 53rd week (not a charge, but a one-off boost): ~$1.63B revenue / ~$490M segment operating income in Q4; ~$0.17 of full-year adjusted EPS. Every year-over-year growth rate in this release is flattered by it.

Restructuring and impairment charges were $317M pre-tax ($0.13/share) — excluded from adjusted EPS, as is acquisition amortization of $337M ($0.13/share). Together they explain the entire $0.26 gap between GAAP EPS ($1.51) and adjusted EPS ($1.77).
A+E sale (~$1.3B cash, Sep 30, 2026): a portfolio sale, not operating income; it sits in investing cash flow, not in the quarter's earnings.

Fubo and NFL Transactions: both closed during fiscal 2026 and are now inside the consolidated results — they add revenue and operating income, but also minority-interest deductions and inter-segment eliminations, so the "growth" they contribute isn't clean organic growth. The release attributes ~2 ppts of revenue growth and ~1 ppt of segment operating income growth to them.

Fiscal 2025 tax benefit: the full-year GAAP EPS decline (−18%) is an artifact of a $1,428M income-tax benefit booked in fiscal 2025, not of weaker fiscal 2026 operations — pre-tax income actually rose 18% for the year.
otherDetail: Other expense of $249M, net — $344M of net interest expense on Disney's debt, partly offset by $95M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.

takeaways.text: Revenue +16%, segment operating income +43% and adjusted EPS +59% all beat guidance. But the 53rd week supplied ~$1.63B of revenue and ~$490M of operating income; without it, growth is still solid (segment operating income ~+10% for the year) but not spectacular. The Q4 FY27 comparison will lap that extra week.
takeaways.title: A genuinely strong quarter — with a calendar asterisk

takeaways.text: Entertainment SVOD operating income more than doubled to $824M, and the segment nearly doubled overall — the streaming turnaround is real. Even so, Experiences produced $2.25B of the $4.97B segment profit, with domestic parks operating income up 36% on record guest numbers and two new cruise ships filling up.
takeaways.title: Streaming finally pays, parks still rule

takeaways.text: The NFL deal (10% of ESPN to the NFL) and the Fubo combination (Hulu Live TV merged in, ~70% owned) both boosted revenue this quarter — and both show up as bigger noncontrolling-interest deductions ($243M, nearly double last year) and bigger eliminations. The A+E sale brought in ~$1.3B of cash. FY27 guidance is confident (double-digit adjusted EPS, ~$11B free cash flow, ~$9B buybacks), but Q1 segment operating income is guided to ~$5.4B with growth weighted to the first half.
takeaways.title: The portfolio keeps getting more complicated

verdict: Disney ended fiscal 2026 with a blowout fourth quarter — revenue up 16% and adjusted EPS up 59% — but roughly a third of the operating-profit growth came from a 53rd week that won't repeat, and the parks, not streaming, still deliver most of the profit.
